passages.heading: Physics and Numerics
passages.why: OpenFOAM's own airfoil validation case uses the Spalart-Allmaras model, the studio's default.

passages.heading: Physics and Numerics
passages.why: The free-stream nuTilda of the validation case is about 4 times the molecular viscosity, the ratio the studio uses by default.

passages.heading: Physics and Numerics
passages.why: The domain is about 1000 chords across for a 1 m chord, far larger than the studio's 30-chord far field.

passages.heading: Physics and Numerics
passages.why: The validation mesh resolves the wall, with the first cell centre at y+ below 1, instead of using wall functions as the studio's default does.

passages.heading: Physics and Numerics
passages.why: OpenFOAM's own airfoil validation writes convection as bounded Gauss linearUpwind, the entry the studio writes; the turbulence line is quoted because the source page splits the momentum line just above it in two (the viewer draws it back on one line).

passages.heading: Physics and Numerics
passages.why: The velocity table gives freestreamVelocity for the inlet and for the outlet of the validation case; the studio's default fixes the velocity on the inlet instead.

passages.heading: Physics and Numerics
passages.why: The pressure table gives freestreamPressure for the inlet and for the outlet; the studio's default fixes the pressure on the outlet only.

context.heading: Overview
context.why: OpenFOAM's case reproduces NASA's 2D NACA 0012 validation case, the one in the catalogue as nasa-tmr-naca0012.

context.heading: Physics and Numerics
context.why: The validation is run at a chord Reynolds number of about 6 million, fully turbulent flow of the kind the studio models.

context.heading: Physics and Numerics
context.why: The validation mesh is a C-grid one cell thick, the same topology as the studio's mesh.
